post_title: Erlewine Archive - Plugging A Torn Outlet Jack Hole
post_content:
Plugging A Torn Outlet Jack Hole

Since joining the Looth Group, when I'm going through my photo library—which dates back into the '80s—I keep an eye out for things that might interest a good many of our members. Some are from magazine articles, but not necessarily complete, some are complete, and some are short "Trade Secrets". Here's what I thought was an interesting fix.

The Problem

Someone caught their foot on the guitar cord plugged into the output jack on this 335 and pulled the cord sideways, ripping the jack sideways and fracturing the top around it pretty badly (don't have a "before" shot).

The Solution

It was bad enough that I filled it with a large circle of maple to be stronger and to look better than glued slivers. The inlaid plug is shaped like this so that it has a lot of glue surface on the inside of the top. It's a piece turned on the lathe. This is the caul that pulled the plug into place. It's a chunk of nylon with a piece of 1/4"-thick felt stuck to it and then a thin piece of Teflon stuck to the felt—to give the caul soft flexibility so it can move a little as it's being tightened into place. I pulled it in with a string. The plug is pre-drilled for the output jack, and very close to that hole is a small hole through which the end of the string is threaded through. I was able to pull the plug in place and poke the rod into it. (Glue is already spread around the flange on the plug). I turned off the threads on the center of the rod so that they wouldn't catch on the caul as it was being pulled into place. The top caul has a thin piece of Teflon sheet, some folded paper napkins, and a clear acrylic caul over that.

The Finish

I'd left the plug slightly proud of the top so that I could pare it flush with the surrounding surface after the glue dried. I had planned to touch up the finish and that's why I wanted to final-fit the plug—as it turned out, my customer said it'd be fine to just make a bigger jack plate and save some money, and that was fine with me!
